title: What agreements are contracts
gist: Agreements are contracts if made by free consent of parties competent to contract, for lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and not hereby expressly declared to be void.

title: Free consent defined
gist: Consent is free when not caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, or mistake under sections 15 to 22.

title: Undue influence and unconscionable bargains
gist: Contract induced by undue influence where one party is in position to dominate will of other and uses position to obtain unfair advantage; burden of proving contract was not induced lies on dominating party.

title: What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not
gist: Consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless forbidden by law, defeats provisions of law, is fraudulent, involves injury to person or property, or court regards it as immoral or opposed to public policy. Unlawful agreements are void.

title: Agreement in restraint of trade void
gist: Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void. Under Indian jurisprudence (Percept D'Mark v. Zaheer Khan, Niranjan Shankar Golikari), post-employment non-compete clauses are strictly void and unenforceable in India, regardless of reasonableness.

title: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings void
gist: Every agreement by which any party is restricted absolutely from enforcing their rights under or in respect of any contract by usual legal proceedings, or which limits the time within which they may thus enforce rights, is void to that extent.

title: Effect of failure to perform at fixed time in contract where time is of essence
gist: When party promises to do something at specified time and fails, contract becomes voidable at option of promisee if intention was that time should be of essence.

title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
gist: Party suffering from breach is entitled to compensation for any loss or damage naturally arising in usual course of things, but not compensation for any remote or indirect loss or damage.

title: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated
gist: Where contract stipulates sum payable upon breach or penalty, party complaining is entitled to receive reasonable compensation not exceeding amount so named, whether or not actual damage proved. Courts in India strike down unconscionable or penal forfeitures.

title: Requirement of tenancy agreement in writing and registration
gist: No person shall let or take on rent any premises except by an agreement in writing, which shall be informed to the Rent Authority jointly by landlord and tenant within two months.

title: Period of tenancy and extension
gist: Tenancy shall be for the period agreed between landlord and tenant. If tenancy ends and premises is not vacated without renewal, tenant is liable to pay enhanced compensation up to twice the monthly rent for first two months and four times thereafter.

title: Cap on security deposit for tenancy
gist: Security deposit to be paid by tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months rent in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months rent in case of non-residential premises. Security deposit shall be refunded to tenant on date of taking vacant possession after lawful deductions. Contracts demanding 6-10 months residential deposit violate the statutory policy ceiling.

title: Revision of rent and mandatory 90-day notice
gist: Revision of rent between landlord and tenant shall be as per agreed terms. If not agreed, landlord must give written notice three months (90 days) prior to the revised rent becoming effective. Tenant has 30 days to accept or issue termination notice.

title: Division of maintenance and repair responsibilities
gist: Landlord is responsible for structural repairs, whitewashing, internal and external electrical wiring. Tenant responsible for routine upkeep, tap washers, minor repairs. If landlord fails to repair after notice, tenant may carry out repair and deduct cost up to one month rent.

title: Eviction and protection against arbitrary removal
gist: Tenant cannot be evicted during currency of tenancy agreement except on grounds specified before Rent Court, such as non-payment of rent for two months, misuse of premises, structural alteration without consent, or landlord bona fide need.

title: Notice period for vacation and early termination
gist: Notice to terminate tenancy must be served in accordance with the tenancy agreement, typically requiring 30 to 60 days written notice. Automatic lock-in clauses of 6 months to 1 year without tenant exit rights are disproportionately one-sided and review-recommended.

title: Prohibition against withholding essential services
gist: No landlord or property manager shall withhold any essential supply or service enjoyed by tenant in respect of premises, including water, electricity, passage, lift, and sanitation. Penalty payable to tenant for illegal disconnection.

title: Definition of 'unfair contract'
gist: Unfair contract means a contract between a manufacturer or trader or service provider and a consumer, having terms which cause significant change in consumer rights, including: (i) requiring excessive security deposits; (ii) imposing disproportionate penalty for breach; (iii) refusing early repayment; (iv) entitling party to terminate unilaterally without reasonable cause; (v) permitting assignment without consumer consent.

title: Unfair trade practice
gist: A trade practice which adopts any unfair method or deceptive practice for promoting sale, supply, or use of goods or services, including misleading statements or refusing to refund amounts after cancellation.

title: Notice requirement before obtaining consent
gist: Data Fiduciary must give Data Principal an accompanying or preceding notice in clear and plain language informing them: (i) personal data to be processed and purpose; (ii) how to exercise rights of withdrawal and grievance redressal; (iii) how to complain to Data Protection Board.

title: Standards of valid consent and right to withdraw
gist: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with clear affirmative action. Any part of consent which violates the Act is invalid. Data Principal has the unconditional right to withdraw consent at any time, and the process to withdraw must be as easy as giving consent.

title: General obligations of Data Fiduciary and security safeguards
gist: Data Fiduciary must protect personal data in its possession by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach. In event of breach, Data Fiduciary must notify the Data Protection Board and each affected Data Principal.

title: Right to correction and erasure of personal data
gist: Data Principal has the right to correction, completion, updating, and erasure of their personal data whose processing is no longer necessary for the purpose for which it was collected. Contracts waiving erasure rights are invalid.

title: Right of grievance redressal for data principles
gist: Data Principal has the right to readily available means of grievance redressal provided by Data Fiduciary, with response required within prescribed period before approaching the Data Protection Board.

title: Compensation for failure to protect sensitive personal data
gist: Where a body corporate possesses, deals or handles sensitive personal data or information (SPDI) in computer resource and is negligent in implementing reasonable security practices causing wrongful loss or gain, it is liable to pay compensation to affected person.

title: Punishment for disclosure of information in breach of lawful contract
gist: Any person who has secured access to material containing personal information under terms of lawful contract, and discloses such information without consent or in breach of contract with intent to cause wrongful loss or gain, is punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 5 lakh rupees.

title: Intermediary exemption and due diligence requirements
gist: Intermediary is not liable for third party information or communication link hosted by it if its function is limited to access and it observes due diligence while discharging duties under the Central Government rules.
